diet.text: Rodents, frogs, lizards, insects, birds and other snakes

overview.text: The North American Racer is a fast, slender, non-venomous snake found across much of the United States and into Canada, Mexico, Guatemala and Belize. Despite its scientific name 'constrictor', it does not usually squeeze its prey.

identification.text: Most are a single plain colour, which gives the subspecies their names: black, brown, tan, blue or green racers.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 50 to 152 cm depending on the subspecies; the record is 185.4 cm.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Much of the United States on both sides of the Rocky Mountains, north into southern Canada and south into Mexico, Guatemala and Belize.

habitat.text: Usually open, grassy places, but also brush, swamps, roadsides and suburbs; in Florida it is the commonest snake in neighbourhoods.

behaviour.text: Fast and very active by day. It hunts mostly on the ground but climbs well and may raid birds' nests.

diet.text: Small rodents and other mammals, frogs, toads, lizards, small turtles, birds and other snakes; young ones eat insects too.

taxonomy.text: There are 11 subspecies, and it is the only species in its genus.

recognise.text: Usually one plain colour (often black, blue or brown).
